document.title: Scroll flows inside Stack; transparent Stacks pass hits through
document.summary: `layout_flow` now places `Scroll` children like any other flowed child, and a last-child Scroll with no main-axis size fills the rest of a sized parent. An unfilled `Stack` stops taking hits itself, and the SDK makes Scroll's position and size optional.
document.why: A fixed header above a scrolling list in one column still needed hand-placed coordinates, because a `Scroll` child kept its own `x`/`y` ([#89](source:s1)).

sources.title: Lay out Scroll as a Stack child (header plus scrolling list column)
sources.gist: Let Scroll participate in Stack flow with an explicit height or fill the rest as last child; decide Stack hit transparency; extend layout_harness.

sources.label: PR #98
sources.gist: Scroll flows in Stack, unfilled Stack is hit-transparent, Scroll props optional, timers example uses the pattern.

lookFor: Subtle: a `Scroll` nested directly in a `Scroll` now flows too, because a Scroll is a column Stack; [#89](source:s1) only names Stack parents, and the nested-scroll fixture in `tests/hit_test_harness.c` was reordered to keep its expectations.
Subtle: tapping the gap inside an unfilled `Stack` that sits in a `Scroll` now returns the Scroll's id instead of the Stack's, so a drag that starts there still scrolls.

groups.title: Scroll in the Stack flow
groups.why: The issue asks for a Scroll that takes its stated main-axis size or fills the rest as the last child ([#89](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `flows()` now accepts `NT_SCROLL`, and `fills_rest()` lets `layout_flow` overwrite a last-child Scroll's fitted main size with what the parent's stated size leaves, which the new `layout_harness` cases pin down.
lookFor: A filling Scroll is first fitted to its content by its own `layout_flow`, then resized by its parent; this is safe only because a Scroll is always a start-aligned column, so its children do not depend on its size.
The fill size is clamped at 0: a 40px-tall column holding a 60px Rect gives its Scroll a 0 height, not a negative one.

groups.title: Hit-transparent Stacks
groups.why: The issue asks whether a Stack should take hits in the gap between its children ([#89](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `hit_test_instance` returns a Stack's id only when it has a fill, and `hit_test_harness` checks both kinds plus the nested-scroll fixture that now flows.

groups.title: SDK contract and docs
groups.why: Authors need to leave out a Scroll's main-axis size to get the fill, and the docs must state the new flow and hit rules.
groups.summary: `VitaScrollProps` gains optional `x`/`y`/`width`/`height`, the reconciler defaults them to 0 for the unchanged native call, and `CONTEXT.md`, the README and the JSDoc describe the flow and hit rules.

groups.title: Timers example
groups.why: The task asks for the header-plus-scrolling-list pattern in one example.
groups.summary: The timers app becomes a sized column whose three demo rows sit above a `Scroll` that fills the rest with a tick log derived from `ticks`.

commits.subject: feat(layout): Scroll flows inside Stack; transparent Stacks pass hits through
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Scroll is now a flowed child of a Stack or Scroll: it takes its stated main-axis size, or, as the last child without one, fills the rest of a parent with a stated size. A Stack without a fill no longer takes hits itself, so taps between its children reach what is behind it. Scroll's x, y, width and height become optional in the SDK. The timers example shows a header above a scrolling tick log.

Fixes #89

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
